items.a: Yes for **recent** use. NSDUH 2025: nicotine/vaping, alcohol, cannabis, other illicit at historic lows. About **two-thirds of seniors** had no past-month use. Lifetime try is still common. Energy drinks (200–300 mg) went **up**.

2022 peak: ~a **classroom a week**. Mostly **fentanyl** in pills that looked like oxycodone or Xanax. Parents say **poisoning**. Deaths fell after. Naloxone and treatment help; Hadland thinks the illicit **supply** may just be less lethal.

items.q: Why leave the parent out of the room?
items.a: Standard from ~11–12. Trials: more disclosure, more return. Safety is the only break. Several states tried to ban it. Grooming/gender panic: a clinician **cannot** talk a kid into a new gender.

items.q: What should a parent actually say?
items.a: Curious questions about school, then **I recommend you don't**. Not basement beer. Not 90s full-stop. Praise the safe-ride call. Keep curfew/car/cash/phone leverage. If you use daily too, that is part of the case.
